verdict.line: You lose short trades before level 3 when Renekton's Fury-empowered W stun-chains you, but you win from level 9 onward once Q's second stack and tank items let you out-sustain him, matching the near-even 47.6% K'Sante win rate over 1406 games.

brief.thesis: K'Sante has no second Q (Ntofo Strikes) stack and no tank items in the first two levels, so Renekton's Fury-fueled W (Ruthless Predator) wins any trade he commits to. Once K'Sante reaches level 3-5 for the Q shockwave pull and later spikes Iceborn Gauntlet into Jak'Sho/Thornmail, the matchup flips — Renekton's damage is capped by Fury generation while K'Sante's resistances keep scaling. The lane is genuinely even on paper (47.6% over 1406 games) because both halves of the fight cancel out.

theirWindow.what: His W (Ruthless Predator) upgrades from a 2-hit, 0.75s stun to a 3-hit slash that destroys your E (Footwork) shield and stuns for 1.5 seconds. If he's already thrown autos and Q (Cull the Meek) into you and his bar is topped, disengage instead of trading.

yourWindow.when: His E (Slice and Dice) on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Slice and Dice sits at 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s by rank. Once he's spent it to engage or reposition he has no gap-closer or escape, so walk in with Q (Ntofo Strikes) stacks and your own E shield to force a trade he can't run from.

start.why: The dominant start here at 87.7% pick with the higher win rate (48.1% over 1474 games) of the two options — the extra sustain outlasts his Q (Cull the Meek) poke while you wait for your 2nd Q stack.

boots.why: 77% pick, 46.4% win rate — flat damage reduction blunts his autos and the extra slash on an empowered W (Ruthless Predator).

core.why: Antiheal cuts directly into his Q (Cull the Meek) lifesteal and Fury-boosted sustain in extended trades.
Cooldown and tankiness to keep Q (Ntofo Strikes) cycling for pulls while you soak his damage.
Stacking resistances turn your late trades from even into unwinnable for him.
This exact order hit 62.5% win rate in the sample — Thornmail punishes his autos on top of Bramble Vest's antiheal.

their team stacks magic burst on top of Renekton's physical pressure and you need the spell shield

runes.keystoneWhy: Procs on your first attack in a trade, healing and growing your max health — built for soaking Renekton's early poke until your Q stacks and items come online.

summoners.why: 77.4% pick and the best win rate pairing (47.7%) — Teleport resets you after losing an early trade and lets you reconnect for side-lane pressure once Iceborn Gauntlet comes online.

playing.title: Track Renekton's Fury bar
playing.detail: His Q and autos build Fury; past 50 his Q heals more and his W becomes a 3-hit, shield-shredding stun. Don't contest a trade into a topped Fury bar.

playing.title: Hold Q for the second stack
playing.detail: Q (Ntofo Strikes, 3.5s cooldown) only pulls on the 2nd hit. Landing both stacks in one engage removes his disengage and turns the trade.

playing.title: Trade after his E lands
playing.detail: Slice and Dice is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s by rank. Once he's used it to engage, he's stuck in melee with no mobility tool — that's your window for Q into W.

playing.title: Don't blind-initiate with W
playing.detail: W (Path Maker) is 14/13/12/11/10s and needs a visible charge-up before the dash, so he can walk out of it pre-6. Save it to punish his E, not to open.

playing.title: Track his ult off his R casts
playing.detail: Both ults share the 120/100/80/80/80s cooldown. His R (Dominus) is a flat transformation with a short heal/burst window; yours knocks him through terrain. Watch his cast timer, not just yours.

playing.title: Rush Bramble Vest first
playing.detail: The Bramble Vest > Iceborn Gauntlet > Jak'Sho > Thornmail order hit 62.5% win rate in the sample — early antiheal directly guts his Fury-stacked Q sustain.

playing.title: Play for the level 9 spike
playing.detail: You're behind in raw stats before Iceborn Gauntlet, so play for freezes and wave control levels 1-5, then look for all-ins once your resistance items land.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and the 47.6% head-to-head win rate over 1406 games are measured from live OP.GG data on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning (Fury thresholds, cooldown windows, ability tells) is my own tactical read, not measured data.
